jsonld.name: D2C Unit Economics Calculator
jsonld.description: Free D2C unit economics calculator. Enter MRP, GST, COGS, fulfilment, RTO and CAC to get CM1, CM2 and CM3 per order, a full monthly P&L with EBITDA and PAT, and the exact break-even volume.

mainEntity.name: What is CM1, CM2 and CM3 in D2C?

acceptedAnswer.text: They are the three rungs of the contribution ladder. CM1 is net revenue minus product cost. CM2 is CM1 minus fulfilment: shipping, gateway fees, packing. CM3 is CM2 minus returns and the cost of acquiring the customer. CM3 is the only one that pays for salaries, rent and profit.

mainEntity.name: How do you calculate break-even units for a D2C brand?

acceptedAnswer.text: Divide total fixed monthly cost, including depreciation, by CM3 per order. If CM3 is negative there is no break-even volume: more orders simply enlarge the loss, and the fix has to come from price, product cost, RTO rate or CAC.

mainEntity.name: Should CAC be adjusted for RTO?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You pay to acquire every order placed, including the ones that come back undelivered. At a 25% RTO rate your effective cost per delivered order is your CAC divided by 0.75, a third higher than the figure in your ad account.
